name: Question 7
problem:
The vector-valued function $f(r,\theta ),$ given by

$$
f(r,\theta )=⟨{r}^{2},\,2r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,\text{_____}⟩
$$

parametrizes the elliptic paraboloid defined in Cartesian coordinates as

$$
x=\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}+{z}^{2}.
$$

By first considering the transformations

$$
x=Z,\,y=2X,\,z=Y
$$

and writing the resulting system in cylindrical polar coordinates, determine the third component of $f.$
worked_solution:
First, substituting the transformations

$$
x=Z,\,y=2X,\,z=Y
$$

into our equation, we get 

$$
Z={X}^{2}+{Y}^{2}.
$$

If $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the cylindrical coordinates of a point and $(X,Y,Z)$ are the corresponding Cartesian coordinates of that point, then we have

$$
X=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,Y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,Z=z.
$$

Substituting this into our equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Z & ={X}^{2}+{Y}^{2} \\ Z & =(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2} \\ Z & ={r}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta ) \\ Z & ={r}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r,\theta ) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨Z,2X,Y⟩ \\  & =⟨Z,\,2r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩ \\  & =⟨{r}^{2},\,2r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $r\in [0,\infty )$ and $\theta \in [0,2\pi ).$

Therefore, the third component of $f$ is $r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .$

Question 7
?

The vector-valued function f(r,θ), given by

f(r,θ)=⟨r2,2rcos⁡θ,_____⟩

parametrizes the elliptic paraboloid defined in Cartesian coordinates as
x=y24+z2. By first considering the transformations x=Z,y=2X,z=Y

and writing the resulting system in cylindrical polar coordinates, determine the third component of f.

a
rsin⁡θ
b
r2cos⁡θ
c
r2cos⁡θ
d
r2sin⁡θ
e
r2sin⁡θ
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, substituting the transformations

x=Z,y=2X,z=Y

into our equation, we get

Z=X2+Y2.

If (r,θ,z) are the cylindrical coordinates of a point and (X,Y,Z) are the corresponding Cartesian coordinates of that point, then we have

X=rcos⁡θ,Y=rsin⁡θ,Z=z.

Substituting this into our equation, we get

Z=X2+Y2Z=(rcos⁡θ)2+(rsin⁡θ)2Z=r2(cos2⁡θ+sin2⁡θ)Z=r2.

Now, for any point (x,y,z) on our surface, we obtain the following:

f(r,θ)=⟨x,y,z⟩=⟨Z,2X,Y⟩=⟨Z,2rcos⁡θ,rsin⁡θ⟩=⟨r2,2rcos⁡θ,rsin⁡θ⟩

where r∈[0,∞) and θ∈[0,2π).

Therefore, the third component of f is rsin⁡θ.
